verdict.rationale: Anrok ships its own headless, API-first interface. It markets "Headless Tax" ("Run tax through Anrok's APIs, or hand it to your agents"), authenticates with bearer-token API keys, gives curl examples, and documents rate-limit handling with 429 and Retry-After, so unattended scripted automation is supported. Nothing addresses CI or pipeline use specifically, so that part of the story is unproven. Missing for 10: a CLI or CI/pipeline integration docs, a test/sandbox environment for automated runs, independent hands-on corroboration of headless automation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Run tax through Anrok's APIs, or hand it to your agents. One engine powers all five jobs, and Headless Tax makes it reachable wherever your team already works.
Now that you have a Product ID in Anrok and have generated an API key, you're ready to make your first API request.
API callers would receive an HTTP 429: Too Many Requests response and Integer Retry-After: Number of seconds to wait for the rate limit to reset.
